{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Schoebel Anita.jpg|alt=Anita Schöbel|thumb|Anita Schöbel]]
'''Anita Schöbel''' (born 1969){{r|born}} is a German mathematician and [[operations research]]er known for her work in [[Optimal facility location|facility location]] and [[mathematical optimization]] of timetables for [[public transportation]]. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Kaiserslautern]], where she is head of the optimization group and director of the {{ill|Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics ITWM|lt=Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics|de|Fraunhofer-Institut für Techno- und Wirtschaftsmathematik}}.{{r|nkl}} She is also the president of the [[German Operations Research Society]].{{r|euro}} 

==Education and career==
Schöbel studied mathematics and economics at the University of Kaiserslautern, earning a diploma in mathematics in 1994 and a doctorate ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) in 1998.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Locating Lines and Hyperplanes – Theory and Algorithms'', was jointly supervised by {{ill|Horst W. Hamacher|de}} and Horst Martini.{{r|mg}}

She remained at Kaiserslautern as a researcher in the Traffic Department in the Institute of Industrial Mathematics. She moved to the department of mathematics in 1999, and earned her [[habilitation]] at Kaiserslautern in 2003. Her habilitation thesis was ''Customer-oriented Optimization in Public Transportation''. In 2004 she moved to the [[University of Göttingen]] as a professor,{{r|cv}} and in 2019 she returned to Kaiserslautern as a professor of mathematics and director of the Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics.{{r|nkl|cv}}

==Books==
Schöbel published her dissertation, ''Locating Lines and Hyperplanes: Theory and Algorithms'', as a book with Kluwer in 1999.{{r|llh}} She is also the author of another book incorporating material from her habilitation thesis, ''Optimization in Public Transportation: Stop Location, Delay Management and Tariff Zone Design in a Public Transportation Network'' (Springer, 2006).
